title: "Practice: Planar Systems"
subtitle: "Module 1: Low-Dimensional Dynamics"

This is ungraded practice. You will build a Matplotlib animation for one planar ODE model [@strogatz2024nonlinear; @hunter2007matplotlib]. The goal is to connect the geometry of the phase plane with the time evolution of the solution.

You can use these pages as guides:

[CDIMA: Phase Plane](cdima-phase-plane.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}
[Van der Pol Oscillator](van-der-pol.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}
[FitzHugh-Nagumo Model](fitzhugh-nagumo.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}
[Animations and Interactivity](animation.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}

## Goals

Your work should show that you can:

- simulate a two-dimensional ODE correctly;
- visualize the model in the phase plane and in time;
- interpret nullclines, equilibria, and transient or oscillatory behaviour.

::: {.callout-note}
## Model choice

Choose one model: the [Van der Pol oscillator](van-der-pol.qmd) or the [FitzHugh-Nagumo model](fitzhugh-nagumo.qmd) (Session 9).
:::

## Tasks

- Write one Python script that opens a figure for your chosen model.
- Plot the nullclines and the equilibrium point.
- State whether the equilibrium is stable or unstable.
- Animate one trajectory in the phase plane using a line and a moving point.
- Add a second subplot that animates one variable as a function of time.

Use the pipeline from [CDIMA: Phase Plane](cdima-phase-plane.qmd) as the structural template, and adapt it to your chosen system. Use [Animations and Interactivity](animation.qmd) for the animation logic.

## Short discussion

Include a brief paragraph that answers these questions:

- What qualitative behaviour did your model show: convergence, oscillation or excitability?
- How do the nullclines explain the geometry of the trajectories?
- Which parameter had the clearest effect on the behaviour you observed?

::: {.callout-tip}
## Optional extension
- Make the figure interactive so clicking on the phase plane resets the initial condition.
- Compare two parameter values in the same report.
- Add a short explanation of the fixed-point stability from the Jacobian or the observed flow.
:::

## Tips

- Start with a static phase-plane plot before you animate anything.
- Reuse the CDIMA structure instead of writing the whole script from scratch.
- Test the ODE, nullclines, and fixed point separately.
- Keep the first animation simple, then add labels or interaction.
- Use the model page to decide which variable to show in the time subplot.

::: {.callout-tip}
Reference implementations are available in `amlab/odes_2d/cdima.py`, `amlab/odes_2d/van_der_pol.py` and `amlab/odes_2d/fitzhugh_nagumo.py`.
:::
